The court should apply Washington law and deny the punitive damages claim, because a federal court in Washington uses Washington's choice-of-law rules, and Washington's bar on punitive damages is likely treated as a public-policy rule that can override California's more permissive rule. The shared note's view that California law controls because the accident happened there gives too much weight to one contact, since Washington's most-significant-relationship test also considers the plaintiff's domicile and the forum's policy. I have not verified current Washington decisions on this point, so this rests on general principles.

CONFIDENCE: 55
